text:
Kai: heads-up — observed cluster-autoscaler picking small GPU nodeclasses for burst jobs in eu-west and then failing packing, causing lots of OOMs+evicts. want to propose a preferential-scaling policy for GPU classes (prefer larger vRAM nodes first).
Sarah: can you paste autoscaler flags? iirc we run --expander=least-waste but that seems to choose smallest binfit.
Kai: current flags: `--expander=least-waste --balance-similar-node-groups --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m`
Anya: least-waste favors small nodes to reduce leftover capacity, but for GPU workloads that bins badly (model memory > small-gpu memory). we should bias by node "class" matching gpu.memory label.
Jun: idea: add a custom priority function by node class weight and fallback rules. e.g. prefer nodeclasses: [a100x40, a100x80, v100x32, t4x16] and only fall back if no capacity across regions.
Sarah: how would we implement? CA doesn't support arbitrary ranked lists out of the box. options: 1) maintain separate nodegroups per class and use expander heuristics + weights 2) wrapper that annotates pods with nodeSelector/affinity at admission 3) fork CA to add class-based preference.
Kai: 1) seems pragmatic: create nodegroups with `node.k8s.io/gpu-class=<class>` label and tune `--expander=least-waste` plus nodegroup weights via cluster-autoscaler config? we can also tweak `--scale-up-from-zero` per-group to control warm pools.
Anya: also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups` off; it forces even scaling across groups and can force bringing up many smaller pools. for gpu-heavy jobs, we want concentrated capacity so turn it off for gpu nodegroups.
Jun: we tested three scenarios in sim yesterday:
```
# 1: current
expander=least-waste, balance-similar=true => avg startup 6 nodes (small), 25% evict rate
# 2: prefer-large via nodegroup priority (label weights), balance-similar=false => avg 2 large nodes, 2% evict rate
# 3: add admission affinity => mixes, requires scheduler webhook
```
Sarah: nice. what about scale-down settings? small nodes get created and then linger because unneeded detection is conservative. maybe reduce `--scale-down-unneeded-time` for GPU pools to 5m? but risk thrash.
Kai: we can set per-nodegroup autoscaler profiles? cloud autoscaler doesn't support per-group flags in our managed version. alternative: use node-affinity + PDBs for critical jobs and increase `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` for gpu groups.
Anya: don't forget `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` and `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods` — our gpu nodes run model cache pods with local disk; scale-down sees them as busy. remove caches or mark cache pods as evictable (taint+toleration) so CA can scale.
Jun: also network note: eu-west AZ C sometimes reports capacity depletion in provider API leading CA to erroneously think no large nodes available and choose smaller nodeclasses in another zone. we should add region-level fallback policy and prefer cross-AZ same class rather than downsize.
devops-bot: [AUTO] cluster-autoscaler /metrics shows spike in scale-up events: +34 events last 3h. See https://rdrw.infra/ca/metrics?range=3h
Sarah: next steps: 1) create nodegroups per gpu-class with labels 2) run a canary with `balance-similar=false` for those groups 3) lower scale-down-unneeded for gpu groups in test cluster 4) remove local model-cache PDBs or mark as evictable 5) monitor for cross-AZ capacity fallbacks. anyone want to own the canary?
Anya: i'll own the canary. will spin up nodegroups and run synthetic batch jobs.
Kai: thanks — ping me once the canary is up and i'll run the load generator + eviction sim. will also add a quick doc with recommended flags for gpu nodegroups. :thumbsup:
Sarah: thanks all. save any sim logs here so we can compare against master branch CA behaviour.
